summary: access smoke: broker-level proof that durable deletion flips /readyz (or exits) — end-to-end for TKT-97
description: TKT-97 planning decision #4 (deferred to follow-up, owner-waived gateless run). TKT-97 unit-tested the *reaction* to ConsumeContext.Closed() firing (waitConsume) but not that the nats.go library actually fires Closed() on durable deletion — that needs a live NATS. Add a smoke test in the smoke/ module: start the access consumer against a real JetStream, delete the durable (access-ticket-issuer and/or access-slot-policy) via the NATS API, assert /readyz flips to 503 (or the process exits) within a bound. Larger harness than make check's unit gate (compose orchestration + durable manipulation), which is why it was split out of TKT-97. Confidence today rests on the library's documented Closed() contract (pull.go:803-808) + TKT-97's unit reaction test; this closes the loop end-to-end.
